about: Points marked by hand: read by eye off crops of the original input, each a crop of the stated box (left, top, right, bottom, in the original's pixels) enlarged `zoom` times with a grid every `gridPx` pixels labelled in the original's pixels, the labels in a strip outside the crop. Pixel coordinates are the original's, with (0, 0) the centre of the top left pixel. I1-back is read flipped left to right (its x is 2375 less the file's). Nothing here is moved after a fit; spike.py records what it does to each mark.

scale.what: On I1-front. Rows across: the first and last pin of both rows of the ten ICs and of the expansion header P2, each the middle of the pad as read by eye, then moved to its blob's centroid by common.refine_to_pad (refused beyond 0.6 mm). Pin 1 is at the lower left of each DIP: every DIP lies with its notch to the left. Drills: pin 1 and pin N, directly across from it on the other row, of each IC, the middle of the hole as read by eye, then fitted on the hole's top rim by spike.py.

fingers.note: The end fingers of the component side, a point in the middle of each read by eye. Not refined with common.refine_to_pad, which finds round pads; spike.py puts each between its two edges (finger_centre).

outline.what: On I1-front: the outline's shape, for board_frame.py to measure. The corners in order round the board, clockwise as the scan lies, from the top left; edge i runs from corner i to corner i + 1, and the last back to the first. Each corner is read by eye on its crop to about half a millimetre: it says where to look and where the outline turns, and where each edge lies is measured by board_frame.py on the light, never taken from here. The coordinates were first placed from an automatic trace of the outline by an earlier version of board_frame.py, then each was checked on its crop and moved where it was wrong: corners 0 and 1 down to the routed edge under the break-off tabs' remains (the bottoms of the half holes between them), corners 6 and 7 up to the step's edge from the shadow below it. The round notches are marked by their deepest points and the edge they are in. Edge 0, the short top left stretch, carries the remains of break-off tabs over most of its length, standing about 0.9 mm out, with half holes between them reaching down to the routed edge (the top right stretch has them over its right end only, and its straight part is most of it).

corners.what: top left: the left edge and the routed top edge of the short top left stretch, under its tabs' remains
the short top left stretch's right end, at its routed edge
the step down in the top edge, inside corner
the step back up in the top edge, inside corner
the top right stretch's left end
the right edge's step, outer corner (marked at the dark lower edge of the bare laminate, above the shadow)
the right edge's step, inside corner (as corner 6)
the right slot's right wall at the bottom edge
the right slot's top right inside corner
the right slot's top left inside corner
the right slot's left wall at the bottom edge
the left slot's right wall at the bottom edge
the left slot's top right inside corner
the left slot's top left inside corner
the left slot's left wall at the bottom edge

notches.what: the round notch in the left edge, its deepest point
the small round notch in the right edge, above the step, its deepest point
the small round notch in the right edge, just above the step, its deepest point

solderSeeds.what: Four holes far apart, each the middle of the hole read by eye on I1-front and on I1-back flipped left to right.

palLayout.what: The pins' feet where they meet the board on I3, the PAL NES-CPU-11 (the solder joint or pad of each end pin, not the leg's shoulder: a 20 mm lens leans what is tall), read by eye off crops enlarged twice with a 10 px grid; the same pins on I1-front from its pads, moved by common.refine_to_pad. Pin 1 is at the lower left of each DIP on both boards.
palLayout.crops: I3: for each IC, its four corners, each a crop of 180 by 140 px centred on the pin's place predicted from U6 and U5, enlarged twice with a 10 px grid. I1-front: the scale's tiles, and for the 300 mil rows of U1 and U4, 40 px tiles enlarged eight times with a 5 px grid.

parts.note: Both boards carry two footprints here, 600 and 300 mil, sharing the row of pins 1 to 12; I3's RAM is in the 300 mil one, so its pins 13 and 24 are marked in the 300 mil row on both boards.
Both boards carry two footprints here, 600 and 300 mil, sharing the row of pins 1 to 12; I3's RAM is in the 300 mil one, so its pins 13 and 24 are marked in the 300 mil row on both boards.
Pin 16 is under a capacitor on I3, so U3 is marked by pins 1, 8 and 9 on both boards.

notMeasured.why: On I3 the 72-pin cartridge connector is fitted over the edge fingers, so no finger can be seen.
On I3 the expansion port's socket is fitted; its body hides every pin.
On I3 the PAL modulator's can covers the place of the 5-pin MOD RF footprint that I1 shows; its own pins on its small board above the can are not the board's.

case.what: Each of the case top's four edges marked by hand as a segment along it (two points read by eye off crops enlarged two or three times with a 10 px grid, away from the rounded corners); spike.py fits a line to the edge near each segment and puts each corner where two lines meet. nearLong is the long top edge nearer the camera (the front in O2-FL, the rear in O2-BR), farLong the other, nearShort and farShort the short ones. base is a segment along the bottom edge of the near long face, where the case meets the table. An optional third number is the half width of the search across the segment, in px. verticals are two segments along the corners' vertical edges at the near long face's two ends, between the top and where the bottom shell starts: a check on the camera, not used in the figures.
case.notes: The corners' vertical edges stop where the bottom shell starts: below it the bottom shell's sides lean in, so no corner edge reaches the table. The height is read instead from the bottom edge of the near long face, through the vertical plane of that face (spike.py, case_photo). On O2-BR the near long face's bottom edge is used right of its middle notch only: left of it the edge is broken by the connector panel and the notch.

palFront.what: Lines on the front band of the top shell, each a segment marked by hand along it; spike.py fits each line. O2-FL: the band's ends are the corners' vertical edges, its top the case top's near long edge (from "case"), its bottom where the bottom shell starts, either side of the black strip; the door's left side is the middle of the dark gap beside it, its right side the black strip's left edge; POWER's left edge and RESET's right edge on the bottom shell. O4: the PAL top shell, taken apart, straight on: its band's four edges, the door's left gap and the black block's left edge.

notMeasured.why: O4 is the PAL top shell taken off its console; POWER and RESET are on the bottom shell, which O4 does not show. Measured on O2-FL and the patent, recorded.

patent.what: O1, the design patent: each view a box marked by hand round its drawing, on the PDF page pdfimages takes it from (page 3 is sheet 2, page 4 sheet 3, 2320 by 3408 px at 300 dpi), read off the sheets shrunk three times and checked on crops at full scale. front: lines on FIG 3, the front view, each a place marked by hand on a crop enlarged four times with a 5 px grid, and the run along it that is read: the top shell's two sides, its top and the seam below it (two drawn lines, read together), the door's left side (two lines) and the black strip's left edge (two lines), POWER's left and RESET's right edges (each the middle of the three lines drawn round each button).

footprints.what: On I1-front: each footprint's reference, read by eye off its crop of the print (nothing in the tools reads text): a point inside the footprint (`at`), and where the grouping cannot tell, the pairing of its rows (`rowSpacingMm`, `alternate` for a second footprint sharing a row) or its pin 1 (`pin1`, a point on the pad). A mark with `pins` groups a footprint by hand, pin by pin, each a point on its pad. board_register.py records what each mark did (registration.json "marks").

marks.reason: The print reads 'U6' and 'CPU' above the footprint's upper row at its left, and 'CPU' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U5' and 'PPU' below the footprint's lower row, and 'PPU' inside its outline.

The print reads 'U2' and '74LS373' below the footprint's lower row, and '74LS373' inside its outline. Pin 1 by hand: the print's notch is at the outline's left end, but a via sits in it and another beside it, and the print is not looked for within 1 mm of a hole, so the grouping cannot see enough of it; pin 1 is at the lower left, task 0's mark.
The print reads 'U3' and '74LS139' below the footprint's lower row, and '74LS139' inside its outline.

The print reads 'U7' and '40H368(CI)' above the footprint's upper row, and '40H368(CI)' inside its outline. Pin 1 by hand: a via sits in the outline's notch at its left end, so the grouping cannot see the notch; pin 1 is at the lower left, task 0's mark.
The print reads 'U8' and '40H368(CII)' below the footprint's lower row, and '40H368(CII)' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U10' and 'CIC' above the footprint's upper row, and 'CIC' inside its outline.
The print reads 'U9' and '74HCU04P' below the footprint's lower row, and '74HCU04P' inside its outline (the KiCad redrawing has a 74LS04 here; the scan wins, as the plan's Facts say).

The print reads 'U1' and 'SRAM(WRAM)' below the footprint's lower row. Three rows of 12 holes: the 600 mil footprint is the upper and the lower row (the plan's Facts: U1, the 6116, is a DIP-24 at 600 mil; task 0's scale marks take these two rows), drawn as a dashed outline above a solid one; the middle row and the lower are a 300 mil footprint for a narrower RAM (the PAL board's sit there, task 0). The grouping could pair the lower row either way, so the pairing is said here. The 600 mil outline has no notch at its middle, where the middle row runs; pin 1 is at the lower left, the corner the narrow outline's notch marks and where every DIP on this board has its pin 1 (task 0's marks).

U1's 300 mil footprint: the middle row and the lower row, inside the solid outline whose notch is at its left end. Kept as an alternate, sharing the lower row with U1. Pin 1 by hand: the notch at the outline's left end runs beside the middle row's first hole, which is not found, so the grouping cannot see enough of it; pin 1 is the lower row's left end, as for U1.

The print reads 'U4' and 'SRAM(VRAM)' below the footprint's lower row. Three rows of 12 holes, as at U1: the 600 mil footprint is the upper and the lower row (the plan's Facts: U4, the 6116, a DIP-24 at 600 mil), the dashed outline above the solid one; pin 1 at the lower left, as at U1.
U4's 300 mil footprint: the middle row and the lower row, inside the solid outline whose notch is at its left end. Kept as an alternate, sharing the lower row with U4.
The edge fingers. The print reads '1' above the left end finger and '36' above the right end finger, so pin 1 is the component side's left end finger.

The expansion connector: two rows of 24 on 2.54 mm, about 6.3 mm apart, which no DIP spacing fits. The rows' end pins are task 0's scale marks. The print reads '48' at the upper row's left end, '25' at its right, '1' and '24' below the lower row's left and right ends, and 'P2' below it, so pin 1 is the lower row's left end and pins 25 to 48 run back along the upper row. The grouping found only parts of the upper row (holes there are not all found on either face).

The RF modulator: five large rings 4 mm apart below the print's 'MOD RF' strip, which reads '5' above the right end, so pin 1 is the left. The modulator's can is held by tabs in slots, which are not round holes and are not grouped here.

A controller header: seven holes 2.0 mm apart in an outline, the print reading '7' at the left end and 'P4' with '1' at the right (P41 at the half-size view), so pin 1 is the right end. Its pitch is not 2.54 mm, which the grouping's rows on 2.0 mm found, unnamed.
The other controller header: seven holes 2.0 mm apart down the board, the print reading 'P5' and '7' at the top, so pin 1 is the bottom end (read on a second crop below the first).
Power and reset: five large rings down the right edge, four 5 mm apart and the bottom one 7.5 mm further, so grouped pin by pin. The print reads '5' beside the top ring, so pin 1 is the bottom.

The crystal: the print reads 'X1' and 'X'tal' beside an outline lying on the board; its two leads are the two holes at the outline's left (upper first), and the two holes at its right corners hold the can down. No pin numbers are printed; the order is the leads, upper first, then the can's two, upper first.
The 4 MHz resonator: three holes 2.5 mm apart down the board in an outline, the print reading '3', 'X2' and '1' beside it from the top, so pin 1 is the bottom.
